rows.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
rows.text: A door of mass \(M\) and width \(L\) is hinged at one end and rotates about a vertical axis without friction. A bullet of mass \(m\) \((m \ll M)\) fired perpendicularly to the door at a speed \(v\) gets embedded in it at a distance \(x\) from its axis of rotation. Assuming the door was stationary initially, how does the resultant angular speed \(\omega\) of the door vary as a function of \(x\)?
options: Graph of \(\omega\) against \(x\): a straight line rising from the origin to its highest value at \(x = L\), then dropping vertically to zero and staying at zero beyond \(L\).

Graph of \(\omega\) against \(x\): a curve rising from the origin, steep at first and flattening out (concave down), up to \(x = L\), then dropping vertically to zero and staying at zero beyond \(L\).
Graph of \(\omega\) against \(x\): a curve rising from the origin, slowly at first and steepening (concave up), up to \(x = L\), then dropping vertically to zero and staying at zero beyond \(L\).

Graph of \(\omega\) against \(x\): zero from the origin up to \(x = \frac{L}{3}\), then a curve rising steeply and flattening out (concave down) up to \(x = L\), then dropping vertically to zero and staying at zero beyond \(L\).

rows.subtopic: Velocity, Acceleration and Force Law in SHM
rows.text: A body of mass \(m\) executes simple harmonic motion along a line with time period \(T\) and energy \(E\). What is the magnitude of the maximum acceleration of the body?

rows.subtopic: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion
rows.text: An athlete runs on a straight track. She starts from rest and runs with a constant acceleration for the first 2 seconds, reaching a speed of \(9\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). She then continues at this constant speed for some time before slowing down to a halt at a constant deceleration. The total time taken, from start to finish, is 12 seconds. If the magnitude of her acceleration is twice the magnitude of deceleration, then what is the total distance covered by her?

A capacitor of capacitance \(C\) consists of two large parallel metal plates. The coefficient of linear expansion of the metal is \(\alpha\). What is the change in capacitance if the temperature of the plates rises by \(\Delta T\), while the gap between the plates is kept fixed?
What are the charges stored in the \(2\,\mu\mathrm{F}\) and \(4\,\mu\mathrm{F}\) capacitors in the given circuit a long time after the key K is closed?

figure.note: A rectangular circuit with three horizontal branches between a left vertical wire and a right vertical wire. Top branch: resistor labelled 4 k then resistor labelled 2 k in series. Middle branch: capacitor labelled 2 µF then capacitor labelled 4 µF in series (no connection between the middle of this branch and the top branch). Bottom branch: resistor labelled 2 k, a cell labelled 12 V, and resistor labelled 4 k in series. A key labelled K sits in the left vertical wire between the middle branch and the bottom branch.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Force and Motion in a Magnetic Field
rows.text: Consider a point charge \(+q\) moving with a constant velocity \(\vec{v} = v\hat{k}\) in vacuum in the presence of an electric field \(\vec{E} = E_x\hat{i} + E_y\hat{j}\) and a magnetic field \(\vec{B} = B_x\hat{i} + B_y\hat{j}\). Unit vectors \(\hat{i}\), \(\hat{j}\), and \(\hat{k}\) are in the directions of \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) axes, respectively. Which of the following relations is correct?

rows.subtopic: Potential Energy of a System of Charges
rows.text: Four point charges \(q\), \(-2q\), \(-3q\) and \(4q\) are placed at the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron of side \(L\), while a charge \(5q\) is placed at its center. What is the total electrostatic energy of the system? (Vacuum permittivity is denoted by \(\varepsilon_0\).)
The half life of a radioactive element is 2000 hours. Approximately how much time is required for the decay of 2/3 of its nuclei?

rows.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
rows.text: A 2-input exclusive OR (XOR) gate with inputs \(X\) and \(Y\) produces the output \(\bar{X}Y + X\bar{Y}\). In the Boolean circuit shown below, which values of the inputs \(P\) and \(Q\) will produce the output 0?

figure.note: An XOR gate (labelled XOR) with inputs 1 and P, and an AND gate (labelled AND) with inputs 1 and Q. The two gate outputs feed the two inputs of a NAND gate (labelled NAND), whose output is labelled 0.

rows.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
rows.text: In an experiment on the photoelectric effect, the de Broglie wavelength of the emitted electron is \(\lambda_B\). The energy of the photon incident on the metal is five times the work function. If \(h\) is Planck's constant and \(m_e\) is the electron mass, then what is the work function?

An ambulance traveling at a speed \(20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) emits a sound of frequency \(540\ \mathrm{Hz}\) from its siren. Sunanda is driving a car which approaches the ambulance from the opposite direction at a speed of \(20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). What will be the change in detected frequency by Sunanda, as she crosses the ambulance? (Given, the speed of sound in air is \(340\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).)

Consider a Young's double slit experiment with monochromatic light of wavelength \(600\ \mathrm{nm}\). The intensity of the light is \(I_0\) at a point on the screen where the path difference is \(600\ \mathrm{nm}\). What would be the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is \(100\ \mathrm{nm}\)?

rows.subtopic: Kinetic Theory of an Ideal Gas
rows.text: Consider a mixture of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) and \(\mathrm{N_2}\) gases at temperature \(27\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}\). Which of the following relations is correct?
options: RMS speed of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) molecules \(<\) RMS speed of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) molecules
Average kinetic energy of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) molecules \(<\) Average kinetic energy of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) molecules
Average kinetic energy of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) molecules \(>\) Average kinetic energy of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) molecules
RMS speed of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) molecules \(>\) RMS speed of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) molecules
